title: Declare rule as a registry-first addressable kind over rules.toml
description:
With rule names in `.jit/rules.toml` colon-free, `rule` can be declared as a project-scope, registry-first item kind so each rule resolves at its `@/rule/<self-id>` address alongside the other kinds already declared under `[item_kinds]` (`.jit/config.toml:104-146`) — in particular the existing `[item_kinds.invariant]` entry, which is sourced from `.jit/invariants.toml` via the same generic `TomlSourceDescriptor` mechanism (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:589-608`, `crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs:1086-1139`, `load_toml_scope_items`/`project_toml_entry`).

Add `[item_kinds.rule]` to the live `.jit/config.toml`, mirroring the `invariant` kind's shape:
```
[item_kinds.rule]
section = "success_criteria"
id-pattern = "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*"
markers = []
link-namespaces = []
scope = "project"
source = { toml = ".jit/rules.toml", table = "rules", id-field = "name", text-field = "<chosen-field>" }
source-of-truth = "registry-first"
```
`section`/`id-pattern`/`markers` are required by `validate_item_kinds` for every declared kind but are not enforced at index time for a registry-first project-scope kind (`domain/item.rs:1117-1122`), so any valid placeholder works. `rules.toml` entries have no natural free-text field (unlike `invariants.toml`'s `statement`); pick a pragmatic `text-field` source (e.g. reuse `name`, or add a short `description` column to each entry) — the choice is not prescribed, only that the projected item's text is non-empty.

Add the same `[item_kinds.rule]` block to the `jit init` scaffold template (`crates/jit/src/hierarchy_templates.rs`, alongside the existing `[item_kinds.invariant]` block around line 205) so newly-initialized repos get the `rule` kind out of the box, and extend the golden/resolution tests that pin that template's `[item_kinds]` table (`hierarchy_templates.rs:467-524`, `test_generated_config_emits_item_kinds_table_golden`, `test_generated_config_item_kinds_resolve_with_no_built_ins`) to include `rule` in the expected block and kind-name list.

Verify resolution end to end: add a test analogous to `test_show_item_resolves_invariant_by_qualified_id` (`crates/jit/src/commands/item.rs:856`) but for the `rule` kind, resolving one of the migrated colon-free rule ids (e.g. `coverage-preview` or `label-format`) through the project's item-resolution path and asserting it returns that rule's projected item with a non-empty self-id and text.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: `.jit/config.toml` declares `[item_kinds.rule]` as a project-scope, registry-first kind sourced from `.jit/rules.toml`'s `rules` table via a `TomlSourceDescriptor`.
- [hard] REQ-02: the `jit init` scaffold template (`hierarchy_templates.rs`) emits the same `[item_kinds.rule]` block, and its golden and kind-resolution tests are updated to include `rule`.
- [hard] REQ-03: a test demonstrates the rule item kind's project-scope address for a migrated colon-free rule id (e.g. `coverage-preview`) resolves to that rule's projected item (non-empty self-id and text).
- [hard] REQ-04: `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.
